articleTitle: RAD or TRAD or both? The future of software development
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Will Tickit and ISO 9000 Survive Rapid Application Development?
abstract: Consideration is given to differing viewpoints about rapid applications development (RAD) and traditional software development methods (TRAD). Traditional methods focus on functionality, on completeness, on correctness. RAD methods focus on speed, on adaptability, on evolution. These descriptive words hold the key to identifying the kinds of circumstance under which it is appropriate to use each method. Traditional methods are appropriate when it only makes sense to complete the analysis of requirements before proceeding to the design stage and when it only makes sense to complete the whole design before moving on to coding and testing. RAD methods are appropriate when it is difficult to articulate the business requirements up front or when these requirements are subject to frequent change. It is clear that powerful results can be obtained from combining RAD and traditional methods in the same development community. This makes the adversarial nature of most RAD vs. TRAD debates so destructive and counter productive. As a consequence and in conclusion, the only statement that really holds true about RAD and traditional methods is the following. The software house that learns to mix and match both RAD and traditional approaches appropriately can beat the world.

articleTitle: The TickIT assessor's guide to RAD
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Will Tickit and ISO 9000 Survive Rapid Application Development?
abstract: A discussion is given on rapid application development and its compliance with ISO 9000 and TickIT standards. There are a number of principles which an assessor would use in looking for evidence of compliance with these standards, including: quality policy; organisation; resources; quality system procedures and planning; contract; design planning, output and review; product traceability; process control; inspection and test status; and control of quality records.

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Will Tickit and ISO 9000 Survive Rapid Application Development?
abstract: Once it is properly understood as a rigorous process, there are good reasons to believe that RAD (Rapid Application Development) is a positive boon to producing high quality, well engineered software systems that accurately meet users' requirements. The question is not whether RAD and quality fit comfortably together, but how. The paper considers RAD and quality fundamentals, the Dynamic Systems Development Method (DSDM) and software quality standards.
